  "per_column": [
    {"name": "visit_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.9, "source_groundedness": 0.95, "rationale": "A clean categorization of the reason for visit (preventive, acute, chronic, emergency) that directly relates reasons to urgency/duration. Values match source text well (annual exam→preventive, cough→acute, MI follow-up→chronic)."},
    {"name": "primary_clinical_category", "analytical_usefulness": 0.9, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "Organ-system/clinical grouping gives a strong new axis for grouping reasons. Values are well-grounded; the annual-exam row mapped to endocrine_metabolic is defensible given HbA1c/lipid focus though arguably preventive."},
    {"name": "symptom_acuity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "Severity gradient is a useful mediator between reason and urgency/duration and distinct from the original urgency field. Values track the text (mild fatigue→mild, asymptomatic follow-up→asymptomatic, moderate acne→moderate)."},
    {"name": "condition_complexity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "New vs known/stable/worsening adds analytical leverage for duration/urgency modeling. Well grounded (stable MI→known_stable, worsening acne→known_worsening)."},
    {"name": "injury_mechanism", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Etiology axis is useful, but this is essentially duplicated by injury_or_illness_mechanism, reducing marginal value. Values are reasonable readings of the text."},
    {"name": "diagnostic_workup_intensity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Workup level plausibly correlates with duration, a useful axis. High NULL count is acceptable as 'not stated'. Values grounded (labs→basic_labs, MRI→imaging_ordered)."},
    {"name": "treatment_intensity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Useful for duration/urgency, but somewhat inferential and prone to overreach. The tennis-knee row labeled procedural_in_office is not supported by the text, which only mentions MRI ordered—an invented treatment."},
    {"name": "disposition_signal", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.7, "rationale": "Disposition is a reasonable outcome axis, but often not stated in the text and thus inferred. 'discharge_with_followup' for the acne row is plausible but not explicit; some confident specifics exceed source support."},
    {"name": "patient_age_proxy", "analytical_usefulness": 0.35, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Largely redundant with the original age_group column and heavily dominated by 'adult' (near-constant), giving little new analytical leverage. Values are mostly reasonable but partly inferred from department (Pediatrics→toddler)."},
    {"name": "injury_or_illness_mechanism", "analytical_usefulness": 0.4, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Near-duplicate of injury_mechanism with nearly identical distribution; a mere restatement adding minimal new leverage. Values themselves are well grounded."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.72,
  "source_groundedness": 0.83,
  "rationale": "Most added columns provide genuine new axes (visit_type, clinical_category, symptom_acuity, condition_complexity, workup intensity) that directly serve the query relating reasons to urgency and duration across department/age. Groundedness is generally solid, matching source readings. Weaknesses: two mechanism columns are near-duplicates, patient_age_proxy is largely redundant with the existing age_group and near-constant, and the inferential columns (treatment_intensity, disposition_signal) occasionally assert specifics beyond what the text supports (e.g., a procedural treatment for a knee row that only mentions MRI ordered). Per scope rules, no penalty applied for missing columns."
}
